docs.title: How Registry classifications work
docs.text:
The Registry makes area-specific project classifications before a field visit when the documentary record is strong enough to do so. A site does not have to be litigated before the project can classify it.

The classification is a research conclusion, not a claim that a court has adjudicated that exact address.

docs.title: Three separate questions
docs.text:
Every Registry entry keeps these questions apart:

  1. Forum classification — what constitutional forum category best fits the defined area?
  2. Activity / claimed restriction — what protected activity is at issue, what restriction does government claim applies, and has that restriction actually been constitutionally validated?
  3. Field verification — is a current sign, boundary, door, counter layout, or other physical fact still worth checking?

A pending field check does not automatically downgrade a forum classification. It matters only when the missing physical fact could plausibly change the legal answer.

docs.title: Classification labels
docs.text:
TPF — Traditional public forum Streets, ordinary municipal sidewalks, parks, and sufficiently close analogues. Restrictions receive the highest forum scrutiny.

LPF — Limited public forum Government property intentionally opened for defined speakers, subjects, or purposes. Restrictions may track the forum's purpose but must remain viewpoint neutral.

NPF — Nonpublic forum Government property used for a governmental purpose and not opened for public discourse. Restrictions still must satisfy the applicable reasonableness and viewpoint-neutrality rules.

NOT PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE Employee-only, secure, operational, or otherwise restricted areas outside the ordinary public-access channel.

UNRESOLVED A missing fact or legal authority could realistically change the classification. This is not shorthand for prohibited.

docs.title: Confidence labels
docs.text:
HIGH means the site facts are sufficiently established and controlling or very close authority supports the classification.

MEDIUM means the classification is the project's best current application of controlling doctrine, but a closer case or an outcome-determinative physical fact could change it.

LOW is reserved for tentative classifications that should not be presented as field-ready.

The Registry should use UNRESOLVED, rather than a low-confidence guess, when the missing issue is genuinely outcome-determinative.

docs.title: What the label means in practice
docs.text:
A Registry classification should help answer what kinds of expression fit the forum, not merely name a level of scrutiny.

The practical shorthand is:

  • TPF: general peaceful expressive activity has the strongest forum baseline, subject to valid time/place/manner, safety, permit, and other rules.
  • LPF: expression is protected within the speaker/topic/activity channel the government actually opened.
  • NPF: there is no general right to convert the property into an unrelated expressive venue, but First Amendment protection does not disappear and an actual restriction still must be analyzed.
  • Recording in any forum: forum status alone never answers the camera/microphone question.

The core guide's What Can I Actually Do in Each Forum? matrix separately addresses speech, signs, leaflets, petitioning, demonstrations, solicitation, photography/video/audio recording, public comment, tabling, expressive clothing, and press/information gathering.

docs.title: Constitution First restriction status
docs.text:
The Registry treats rule existence and rule validity as different facts.

A sign, policy, statute, ordinance, contract term, employee instruction, or police order is stored as a claimed restriction until the applicable constitutional and statutory tests have been run.

Every subarea now carries at least one structured restriction_audit. Current statuses include:

  • NO MATERIAL RESTRICTION LOCATED — the current record does not establish a material restriction for that activity; this is not government-granted permission.
  • RULE LOCATED UNTESTED — the rule exists, but constitutional validity has not yet been established.
  • CONSTITUTIONALLY SUPPORTED — authority strongly supports the defined restriction/application.
  • CONSTITUTIONALITY UNRESOLVED — a real legal or factual gap prevents a responsible conclusion; unresolved is not presumed valid.
  • FACIALLY SUSPECT — the text itself presents a substantial constitutional problem.
  • AS-APPLIED SUSPECT — the text may have valid applications, but the documented enforcement appears constitutionally problematic.
  • LIKELY INVALID — controlling authority strongly contradicts the defined restriction/application.
  • UPHELD BINDING — controlling authority supports the materially same restriction/application.
  • NOT APPLICABLE — no public-expression restriction audit is being asserted for that row.

The governing project principle is Constitution First. The detailed testing method is Restriction Audit.

docs.title: Indoor public common spaces
docs.text:
For lobbies, foyers, waiting areas, public service counters, shared corridors, and similar interiors, the Registry separates:

  1. public access;
  2. forum classification;
  3. privacy/confidentiality context;
  4. the facility's own safeguard duties;
  5. duties that actually apply to the visitor;
  6. recording posture; and
  7. the constitutional status of any claimed recording restriction.

The governing rule is:

A facility's duty to protect confidential information is not automatically delegated to a lawful visitor. Privacy can justify a restriction only through the law and constitutional test that actually apply.

HIPAA must be handled with particular care. An ordinary visitor does not become a HIPAA covered entity or business associate merely by entering public common space. If a facility invokes HIPAA, the Registry should separately establish whether the entity is covered, what PHI is actually at risk, what safeguards the entity uses, what rule is imposed on the visitor, and whether that rule independently survives constitutional analysis.

See Indoor Public Common Spaces.

docs.title: Recording is a separate layer
docs.text:
Forum status does not itself answer whether recording is permitted.

A TPF does not eliminate otherwise valid privacy, safety, obstruction, or narrowly tailored conduct rules. An NPF does not manufacture a camera prohibition that the agency has not adopted.

The Registry therefore states recording posture separately, for example:

  • No general public-facing camera ban located
  • Activity-specific device rule verified
  • Officer recording receives strong activity-specific protection
  • Privacy/confidentiality facts may support a narrower restriction
  • Recording rule unresolved

docs.title: Historical enforcement and Rights-Risk Signals
docs.text:
The Registry does not stop at current policy text. Where records permit, it also asks whether government has previously warned, removed, excluded, detained, cited, arrested, prosecuted, or chilled people engaged in the same or materially similar activity.

This historical layer is deliberately separate from the current restriction audit.

A facility can therefore show, for example:

  • a current rule that has been corrected;
  • a historical enforcement event under the superseded rule;
  • a later court decision or policy change; and
  • a current Rights-Risk Signal reflecting the evidence that remains relevant today.

The current scoped signal values are:

  • NONE — a completed review located no material rights-risk in the stated scope and period; absence of a signal is not the same as NONE.
  • POSSIBLE — a concrete issue exists, but the present evidence does not yet document the relevant enforcement or chilling event.
  • DOCUMENTED — reliable evidence documents a material warning, coercive action, enforcement event, or chilling/compliance event involving protected or potentially protected activity. This does not mean a court found the government action unlawful.
  • ADJUDICATED — a court or competent tribunal actually held the relevant challenged policy or enforcement unlawful on the represented issue.

Historical events also carry a date-sensitive legal assessment so the Registry does not judge old conduct solely by later law.

The Registry can therefore surface a pattern that otherwise disappears from case reporters: a person may have stopped leafleting, recording, petitioning, or other protected activity after a government warning and never been arrested or prosecuted. A documented chilling event still belongs in the evidentiary history even though no criminal case followed.

docs.title: Field testing is verification, not a prerequisite
docs.text:
A field visit can be extremely useful for:

  • exact ROW / property transitions;
  • entrance and queue geometry;
  • current signs;
  • controlled-door boundaries;
  • counter privacy;
  • reserved or employee-only parking;
  • actual use inconsistent with old plans or written policy.

But the project does not wait for someone to provoke an enforcement encounter before assigning a classification that the law and documentary facts already support.

The hardening rule is:

Classify now when the missing field fact cannot reasonably change the result. Keep only outcome-determinative uncertainty unresolved.

docs.title: Primary classification anchors
docs.text:
The current pilot Registry relies especially on:

  • Prigmore v. City of Redding, 211 Cal.App.4th 1322 (2012), for library exterior areas and California's area-comparison approach;
  • Faith Center Church Evangelistic Ministries v. Glover, 480 F.3d 891 (9th Cir. 2007), for library meeting-room limited-public-forum analysis;

These rows separate a facility's privacy/confidentiality duties from duties that actually apply to a visitor. A privacy interest can support a narrower restriction, but it does not become a blanket camera ban merely by being asserted.

docs.title: California Final Adversarial Qualification Review
docs.text:
Issue: #82

This is the distinct adversarial review required after closure of GAP-01 through GAP-08 and canonicalization of NC-STANDING-01 v1.

It is deliberately not a "make the matrix green" pass.

The review asks whether the present California overlay can responsibly run the canonical ordinary scenarios while preserving:

  • genuine uncertainty;
  • authority hierarchy;
  • contrary authority;
  • procedural posture;
  • local/facility dependencies;
  • changed-fact branches; and
  • the separation between policy existence and legal/constitutional validity.

This review does not count as the independent qualified human reviewer required by CA-GATE-09. AI-assisted review may support the record but cannot be represented as the missing independent human.

docs.title: CA-F4.5 — current remain/leave/reentry/prospective exclusion posture
docs.text:
Status retained: Researched-Unresolved.

The ordinary access/current-remain branches are runnable. The unresolved edge is narrower:

whether an individualized prospective ban, by itself, makes an otherwise generally open property "not open to the general public" for Penal Code § 602(o).

Published Ninth Circuit Blankenhorn uses conditional language in a private-shopping-center/probable-cause posture. California federal district applications do not supply one controlling state-law answer for an otherwise public-facing government facility.

A fresh adversarial check of People v. Hsiung, A169697 (Cal. Ct. App. 2026) did not resolve this edge. The § 602(o) First Amendment discussion is in Part III, and the Court of Appeal's May 12, 2026 publication order expressly excluded Part III from publication. The existing handbook caution treating that discussion as nonprecedential is therefore correct.

Source: https://law.justia.com/cases/california/court-of-appeal/2026/a169697m.html

No promotion to Supported and no new Gap is warranted.

docs.title: CA-F5.8 — identification request versus legal duty
docs.text:
Status retained: Researched-Unresolved.

The review reconfirmed the important resolved propositions:

  • no general California pedestrian carry-ID statute equivalent to Nevada's Hiibel statute has been identified;
  • refusal cannot manufacture reasonable suspicion where individualized suspicion is otherwise absent;
  • Terry detention alone does not authorize a generalized patdown for identification;
  • false identification, citation/release, driver, arrest, and booking rules are separate;
  • published California cases protect mere refusal/silence in multiple prebooking contexts while allowing changed conduct/booking-stage consequences.

The narrow unresolved edge remains the effect of refusing affirmative identification during every otherwise lawful California Terry detention, especially when older production cases are considered alongside Vanegas's qualified-immunity treatment.

The review does not convert a qualified-immunity holding into a substantive statewide stop-and-identify rule.

No promotion to Supported and no new Gap is warranted.

docs.title: NC-COMPLAINT-01.D — prospective notice / identification
docs.text:
Status retained: Researched-Unresolved.

This branch combines the two genuine California edges above:

  • individualized prior-ban effect under § 602(o); and
  • general otherwise-lawful-detention affirmative-ID duty.

The surrounding decision tree—never entered, entered-and-left, currently remains, prospective notice, reentry, officer reliance, false identity, citation/booking—is supported.

No promotion to Supported and no new Gap is warranted.

docs.title: NC-COMPLAINT-01.I — offered but unreviewed exculpatory recording
docs.text:
Status retained: Researched-Unresolved.

The Ninth Circuit layer supports:

  • investigating the basis of an accusation rather than relying mechanically on an unexamined allegation;
  • accounting for known exculpatory evidence that negates probable cause;
  • dissipation of reasonable suspicion/probable cause as later facts become known; and
  • the effect of objective video actually reviewed.

The current published Ninth Circuit opinion United States v. Holcomb, No. 23-469 (9th Cir. July 17, 2026) reinforces the last proposition: probable cause to continue the challenged search dissipated after investigators actually viewed surveillance video undermining the suspected conduct.

Official Ninth Circuit source: https://cdn.ca9.uscourts.gov/datastore/opinions/2026/07/17/23-469.pdf

The review found no controlling Ninth Circuit rule requiring an officer categorically to watch every recording merely offered before taking otherwise supported action.

The Field Guide therefore correctly preserves the offer/declination as evidence and distinguishes:

actually reviewed / known exculpatory evidence

from

a universal duty to watch every offered recording.

No promotion to Supported and no new Gap is warranted.

docs.title: 4. Authority-hierarchy / posture audit
docs.text:
The Authority Index was reviewed specifically for common overstatement failures.

The following distinctions remain explicit:

  • published Ninth Circuit versus unpublished/nonprecedential memorandum;
  • California Supreme Court / published California Court of Appeal versus federal district-court comparator;
  • out-of-circuit authority as persuasive only;
  • qualified immunity versus substantive law;
  • pleading-stage holdings versus merits holdings;
  • preliminary-injunction/emergency-stay posture versus final merits;
  • statute text versus constitutional validity;
  • policy existence versus lawful authority to adopt/enforce it.

Examples correctly limited in the corpus include:

  • Mackey v. Meyer — unpublished/nonprecedential DMV comparator;
  • Carlson, Langham, Sessions — unpublished device-retention comparators;
  • Wilson — N.D. Cal. pleading-stage comparator;
  • Han, Garcia, James — district-court comparators in the § 602(o) access branch;
  • Index Newspapers — limited preliminary-injunction/stay posture;
  • Vanegas — qualified-immunity holding does not settle substantive § 148 ID law.

No supported matrix row was found to depend solely on a nonprecedential comparator.

docs.text:

rule-maker → enabling authority → required adoption form → actor delegation → preemption → constitutional test → enforcement bridge

It also continues to distinguish:

  • policy/sign/order existence;
  • legal authority to adopt it;
  • internal delegation to the actor enforcing it;
  • constitutional validity;
  • actual criminal/offense elements; and
  • facility-specific facts.

A missing delegation source is recorded as unresolved rather than automatically treated as proof that no authority exists.

No statewide Supported row was found to rely on a local policy as self-validating constitutional law.

docs.title: 1. National baseline contamination check
docs.text:
The canonical national file was reviewed for jurisdiction-specific contamination.

No references were found to:

  • California;
  • the California Penal Code;
  • the California Government Code;
  • the Brown Act;
  • Ninth Circuit doctrine; or
  • California-specific case law.

The national file contains only:

  • jurisdiction-neutral starting facts;
  • allegation-to-elements methodology;
  • identification as a separate legal question;
  • lawful-vantage factual assumptions;
  • complaint-driven, public-meeting, and emergency/assembly factual variants;
  • changed-fact restart rules; and
  • the requirement that jurisdiction overlays supply the actual law.

The file does not declare that:

  • recording is lawful everywhere;
  • a person may ignore a later removal order;
  • identification can never be required;
  • everything visible may always be recorded;
  • peaceful observer status creates immunity from valid dispersal/perimeter law; or
  • the absence of assumed misconduct prevents later changed facts from creating an offense.

docs.title: 2. California overlay separation
docs.text:
The California standing page was rewritten as an overlay.

It now:

  • explicitly inherits NC-STANDING-01 v1;
  • maps neutral facts to California Penal Code and Brown Act branches;
  • keeps California identification doctrine in California;
  • keeps Ninth Circuit recording/police-encounter authority in California;
  • preserves the California allegation-to-elements workflow;
  • preserves California-specific complaint-driven and lawful-vantage consequences;
  • preserves the California public-meeting variant;
  • preserves the California assembly/emergency variant; and
  • keeps later removal orders as new legal facts rather than retroactive trespass.

The California overlay expressly states:

National core supplies the facts. California supplies the law.

docs.title: California Authority Sweep Ledger
docs.text:
Purpose: Make the California Field Guide's completeness work reproducible and auditable.

This ledger records source ranges that have actually been reviewed, what was retained, what was treated as specialized or outside the standing scenario, and what still remains unswept. A completed slice does not mean the entire California code has been completed.

docs.title: Classification labels
docs.text:
• RETAINED — materially relevant to the standing peaceful/public-property audit scenario or to a recurring facility chapter.
  • CONTEXT — does not independently create the principal field rule but materially explains authority, definitions, procedure, or limits.
  • SPECIALIZED — relevant only to a distinct facility/event type and should be handled in that chapter.
  • N/A-STANDING-SCOPE — reviewed but ordinarily requires conduct excluded by the project's standing assumptions or concerns a setting outside the project's ordinary public-facility scope.
  • REVIEW-LATER — text identified, but case law or related provisions must be reviewed before final classification.

For handbook/index status terminology, PRIMARY-TEXT-VERIFIED means current primary text was checked and an initial entry exists. It does not mean the controlling case-law layer is complete. DOCTRINE-REVIEWED is reserved for narrow propositions whose controlling doctrine/material case law have also been reviewed. DOCTRINE-REVIEWED-IN-PART means a narrow part of a broader statutory family has reached that stage while other applications remain unresolved.

The canonical factual baseline for N/A-STANDING-SCOPE and related classifications is maintained in ../california/standing-scenario.md. It expressly excludes unstated fighting, unreasonable noise, obstruction/intimidation, independent § 148 conduct, unlawful-assembly predicates, restricted-area entry, and other unrelated offenses so a sweep does not smuggle hypothetical misconduct into the issue under review.

Every retained authority should ultimately have a direct primary-source link, narrow proposition, important limitations, binding level where applicable, and last_verified date.

docs.title: Sweep 002 — Trespass and property-access family
docs.text:
Review date: September 17, 2026 Detailed ledger: SWEEP-002-TRESPASS-PROPERTY.md
