docs.title: Walnut Creek Library — Exterior Forum Analysis
docs.text:
Facility: Walnut Creek Library Address: 1644 N. Broadway, Walnut Creek, California 94596 Analysis date: 2026-09-22 Principal comparator: Prigmore v. City of Redding, 211 Cal.App.4th 1322, 150 Cal.Rptr.3d 647 (2012) General doctrine: Perry, Cornelius, Grace, Kokinda, Sammartano, Camenzind, and the Field Guide public-forum chapter

Published Prigmore opinion:

https://law.justia.com/cases/california/court-of-appeal/2012/c068866.html

This is an area-specific documentary analysis. It does not assign one forum label to the Walnut Creek Library, its assessor parcel, Civic Park, or the downtown parking system as a whole.

docs.title: 1. Why Walnut Creek is a useful second Prigmore test
docs.text:
Walnut Creek keeps the Contra Costa County Library policy layer substantially constant while materially changing the physical setting from Concord.

Current official evidence shows a downtown civic facility intentionally connected to:

  • a civic plaza at Broadway and Lincoln;
  • a formal Broadway entrance;
  • a Civic Park entrance;
  • a surface parking lot;
  • public-facing outdoor plazas;
  • a large adjoining City civic/park parcel; and
  • an underground garage intended to serve Library patrons, community-center users, and other downtown visitors.

That layout tests whether the project can apply an anchor case by specific area and function, rather than turn library exterior into a categorical answer.

docs.title: Public ownership / civic setting
docs.text:
Official countywide GIS returns:

  • APN 178-300-039 — 1644 Broadway — owner field WALNUT CREEK CITY OF — 2.202 acres;
  • adjoining APN 178-300-040 — 1375 Civic Drive — owner field WALNUT CREEK CITY OF — 7.548 acres.

The human-reviewed assessor sheet independently labels parcels 39 and 40 CITY OF WALNUT CREEK.

City and Library sources describe the Library as being in/adjacent to Civic Park in downtown Walnut Creek.

docs.title: Deliberate public pedestrian access
docs.text:
A City design-period publication states that the new Library would be accessible from:

  1. a new civic plaza at Broadway and Lincoln;
  2. a formal entrance on Broadway;
  3. the surface parking lot; and
  4. a Civic Park entrance.

Source:

https://www.walnutcreekca.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/84/635672432775130000

The City's Public Art Master Plan separately identifies Library Outdoor Plazas and Civic Park walkways/entries as public-art sites.

Source:

https://www.walnutcreekca.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/11536/636136819628970000

docs.title: Public parking
docs.text:
The current CCCL branch page identifies:

  • Library underground garage — 120 spaces, four-hour limit;
  • Library surface lot — 20 four-hour spaces and 10 thirty-minute spaces;
  • nearby Broadway Garage — a separate downtown garage at 1390 N. Broadway.

Source:

https://ccclib.org/locations/26/

The City design publication states that the Library's underground garage was intended for Library patrons, community-center users, and other downtown visitors.

docs.title: Current ROW source family
docs.text:
Walnut Creek Engineering treats sidewalks, curb/gutter and driveway approaches as public-right-of-way work requiring encroachment permits. The City's site-plan standards require depiction of property lines/easements, public ROW, pedestrian/vehicle ingress/egress, parking circulation, street dedications and whether streets are public/private.

Sources:

  • https://www.walnutcreekca.gov/government/public-works/engineering-services/encroachment-permits
  • https://www.walnutcreekca.gov/government/community-development-department/permits/building-permits/site-plans-and-diagrams

Exact surveyed ROW edges at the Library remain unresolved.

docs.title: A. North Broadway municipal sidewalk / actual public-ROW component
docs.text:
Classification: TRADITIONAL PUBLIC FORUM — HIGH CONFIDENCE; EXACT EDGE PENDING WHERE AMBIGUOUS.

An actual ordinary municipal sidewalk is the paradigmatic traditional public forum under Grace, Perry, and Ninth Circuit street/sidewalk doctrine. Walnut Creek's engineering materials establish that public sidewalk/ROW is a City-managed category, while current facility evidence establishes the Library frontage on North Broadway.

The unresolved question is geographic precision at any visually ambiguous transition between street ROW and Library plaza/parcel—not the doctrine applicable once the person is actually on the municipal sidewalk.

docs.title: B. Lincoln Avenue municipal sidewalk / actual public-ROW component
docs.text:
Classification: TRADITIONAL PUBLIC FORUM — HIGH CONFIDENCE; EXACT EDGE PENDING WHERE AMBIGUOUS.

The same rule applies to an identified ordinary municipal sidewalk along Lincoln Avenue. Exact edge work remains available for a location-specific removal/trespass dispute.

docs.title: C. Broadway–Lincoln civic plaza / Library outdoor-plaza area
docs.text:
Classification: TRADITIONAL-PUBLIC-FORUM TREATMENT STRONGLY SUPPORTED UNDER PRIGMORE; CURRENT PHYSICAL VERIFICATION PENDING.

This is an especially close Prigmore comparator because the City itself described the space as a new civic plaza providing access to the public Library, while a separate City plan identifies Library Outdoor Plazas as public-facing civic/public-art locations.

Factors favoring the comparison:

  • City ownership;
  • deliberately open public access;
  • Library-entry function;
  • integration with ordinary downtown pedestrian circulation;
  • adjacency/integration with Civic Park;
  • civic-plaza designation rather than employee/service access;
  • surrounding public art and gathering context.

Current field or equally reliable current imagery should still confirm the exact plaza footprint, seating/congregation features, current signs, and whether any part has been reconfigured or reserved.

docs.title: D. Formal Broadway entrance and immediate approach
docs.text:
Classification: TRADITIONAL-PUBLIC-FORUM TREATMENT STRONGLY SUPPORTED UNDER PRIGMORE; FIELD VERIFICATION PENDING.

The City expressly designed this as a formal public entrance. It performs the same basic entry/circulation function that Prigmore treated as part of the relevant outdoor forum at the Redding library.

This conclusion concerns the open exterior entrance/approach, not the building interior or any security-controlled threshold condition that might exist inside.

docs.title: E. Civic Park entrance / public pedestrian connection between Library and park
docs.text:
Classification: TRADITIONAL-PUBLIC-FORUM TREATMENT STRONGLY SUPPORTED; EXACT LIBRARY/PARK SUBAREA LINE PENDING IF MATERIAL.

The City expressly designed a Civic Park entrance into the Library. On the park side, ordinary public-park doctrine independently supplies a strong traditional-public-forum baseline. On the Library-side connective approach, Prigmore strongly supports forum treatment where the path functions as ordinary public pedestrian circulation between the Library and an adjoining civic park.

The exact parcel line is not outcome-determinative for ordinary peaceful expression if both sides of the transition have the same practical forum result, but should remain available for any location-specific exclusion/trespass dispute.

docs.title: F. Civic Park proper
docs.text:
Classification: TRADITIONAL PUBLIC FORUM — HIGH CONFIDENCE, SUBJECT TO ORDINARY PARK HOURS/RULES AND ANY SPECIFIC RESERVED-USE CONDITIONS.

Public parks are paradigmatic traditional public forums. The Library's adjacency does not convert Civic Park into Library interior property.

Facility-specific park reservations, event permits, closures, or valid content-neutral time/place/manner rules may affect particular conduct without changing the general forum baseline.

docs.title: G. Library surface parking lot
docs.text:
Classification: TRADITIONAL-PUBLIC-FORUM TREATMENT STRONGLY SUPPORTED UNDER PRIGMORE FOR LAWFUL PEDESTRIAN EXPRESSIVE USE; CURRENT LAYOUT/SAFETY CONDITIONS PENDING.

Relevant similarities to Prigmore are substantial:

  • it is expressly Library public parking;
  • it is City-owned civic property;
  • it is one of the Library's deliberately designed access routes;
  • it connects to public entrances/plazas/park circulation;
  • access is not described as an employee-only or secured lot.

As in Concord and Prigmore, parking-lot forum status does not eliminate vehicle, obstruction, parking-duration, driveway, pedestrian-safety, or property-protection rules. The project standing scenario assumes lawful pedestrian positioning without obstructing vehicles or entrances.

docs.title: H. Underground Library garage
docs.text:
Classification: FORUM CLASSIFICATION UNRESOLVED — SPECIAL-PURPOSE / NONPUBLIC-FORUM ANALOGIES MATERIAL; BROAD PUBLIC USE ALSO MATERIAL.

This is where Walnut Creek meaningfully diverges from Concord and from Prigmore.

Facts favoring a broader public-access characterization:

  • CCCL expressly calls it the Library underground garage;
  • 120 public spaces are advertised;
  • the City designed it to serve Library patrons, community-center users, and other downtown visitors;
  • current Oak View materials say it remains accessible for after-hours events.

Facts counseling against simply extending Prigmore:

  • it is an enclosed, purpose-built vehicle-storage/circulation structure;
  • the principal function is parking and vehicle/pedestrian movement, not an open civic plaza or park;
  • safety, access-control, payment, closure, elevator/stair, and event-operation conditions may differ materially from an outdoor public lot;
  • public access alone does not create a public forum.

United States v. Kokinda and Sammartano are useful cautionary comparators for special-purpose government access spaces, but neither decides this garage. The correct result should remain UNRESOLVED until current garage rules, physical layout, pedestrian areas, access/payment conditions, ownership/control, and actual expressive-use evidence are reviewed.

docs.title: I. Underground-garage drive aisles / ramps / vehicle portals
docs.text:
Classification: NO BROAD SPEECH-ZONE CONCLUSION; VEHICLE AND SAFETY FUNCTIONS DOMINATE.

Whatever forum analysis ultimately applies to pedestrian portions of the garage, moving-vehicle lanes and ramps present strong safety and compatibility interests. The standing scenario does not include obstructing vehicle circulation.

docs.title: J. Garage pedestrian exits, stairs, elevators and connective corridors
docs.text:
Classification: UNRESOLVED / SUBAREA-SPECIFIC.

These should not be automatically assigned the garage's eventual classification or the plaza's classification. A stair/elevator landing that is merely a special-purpose transit point may differ from an open plaza at its exit. The exact access sought matters under Cornelius and Kokinda.

docs.title: K. Children's patio
docs.text:
Classification: PURPOSE/ACCESS CONDITIONS REQUIRE SEPARATE REVIEW; NO BROAD EXTERIOR TPF CONCLUSION.

CCCL identifies a children's wing and patio. System children/teen-area rules and the patio's physical relationship to the children's area may materially limit who may use the space and for what purpose. Its outdoor character alone is not enough to assimilate it to the civic plaza.

This is a legal/methodological classification point; it does not depend on any researcher's personal field-practice choice.

docs.title: 4. Comparator matrix
docs.text: Area Principal anchor / doctrine Current documentary posture North Broadway municipal sidewalk Grace / ordinary sidewalk doctrine TPF — HIGH CONFIDENCE; exact edge pending Lincoln municipal sidewalk Grace / ordinary sidewalk doctrine TPF — HIGH CONFIDENCE; exact edge pending Broadway–Lincoln civic plaza Prigmore + civic-plaza facts TPF TREATMENT STRONGLY SUPPORTED Formal Broadway entrance Prigmore TPF TREATMENT STRONGLY SUPPORTED Civic Park entrance/connective path Prigmore + park doctrine TPF TREATMENT STRONGLY SUPPORTED Civic Park proper Perry / park tradition TPF — HIGH CONFIDENCE Surface Library lot Prigmore TPF TREATMENT STRONGLY SUPPORTED; safety limits Underground garage Cornelius / Kokinda / Sammartano cautionary comparison UNRESOLVED Garage ramps/vehicle lanes compatibility/safety NO BROAD SPEECH-ZONE CONCLUSION Garage pedestrian nodes subarea-specific UNRESOLVED Children's patio system purpose/access rules SEPARATE REVIEW REQUIRED

docs.title: 5. Recording-specific consequence
docs.text:
None of these classifications turns Prigmore, Grace, or the park cases into a stand-alone right-to-record decision.

Where the project concludes or strongly supports traditional-public-forum treatment, a recording restriction must then be evaluated under the separate First Amendment/California speech, recording, privacy, and valid time/place/manner doctrines applicable to the actual restriction.

The supported formulation is:

The area's forum status determines the constitutional framework applied to a restriction; it does not itself answer every recording question.

No dedicated public-facing Walnut Creek-specific ordinary-patron photography/videography rule was located in the online sources reviewed as of September 22, 2026.

docs.title: 6. Outcome-determinative boundary gate
docs.text:
The available evidence is sufficient to proceed with forum analysis for several areas without reconstructing a century of title history.

Exact modern engineering lines remain outcome-determinative where:

  • a person stands at a visually ambiguous plaza/municipal-sidewalk transition;
  • a removal order purports to exclude a person from one controller's property but not adjacent ROW/park property;
  • a garage/plaza/park connective space has materially different current control;
  • an easement or reserved-use condition changes lawful public access.

Historical subdivision-map retrieval should not delay the current forum analysis unless one of those concrete questions makes it necessary.

docs.title: 7. Remaining documentary/field work
docs.text:
Highest-value next checks are:

  • current site/engineering plan locating the civic plaza, North Broadway/Lincoln ROW, surface lot, garage entries and Civic Park connection;
  • current signs/rules at the plazas, surface lot and garage;
  • garage pricing, pedestrian circulation, closure/access conditions and any parking-specific conduct rules;
  • current physical plaza/entrance seating and congregation features;
  • control/lease evidence for the cafe and any other separately operated interior/exterior subspace;
  • City rental eligibility/rules for Oak View;
  • current Library-vs-City control allocation where it would change removal authority.

Those remaining questions should be carried as scoped research flags rather than withholding the area conclusions already supported by the documentary record.

docs.title: Facility Prep — Second-Site Validation Checkpoint
docs.text: Facility: Walnut Creek Library Date: 2026-09-22 Branch: field-guide/sweep-08-walnut-creek-library

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Test whether the Facility Prep architecture developed at Concord Library survives a second Contra Costa County Library branch with materially different municipal GIS coverage, parcel geometry, assessor notation, civic context, and public-access subareas.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
SECOND-SITE VALIDATION SUCCESSFUL, WITH MODULARIZATION REQUIRED.

The core evidence pipeline transferred successfully, but the test exposed assumptions that correctly remain jurisdiction/source-specific.

docs.title: What generalized successfully
docs.text:
The second site successfully completed:

facility address → official countywide parcel match → APN → current owner/address fields → parcel geometry → GIS intersection candidates → assessor-map download/hash → human assessor review → recorded-map-index follow-up → relevance screening → area-specific legal analysis

Walnut Creek parcel result:

  • APN 178-300-039;
  • owner field WALNUT CREEK CITY OF;
  • 2.202 acres;
  • Assessor Book 178 Page 30;
  • facility-relevant adjoining City parcel 178-300-040, 1375 Civic Drive, 7.548 acres.

docs.title: Concord AddressPoint
docs.text:
Concord's AddressPoint enrichment is not a countywide address resolver. Walnut Creek required a countywide parcel-address search instead.

Architecture consequence:

a countywide parcel core may be reusable even when municipal AddressPoint/road/owned-property enrichment remains city-specific.

docs.title: Road/ROW enrichment
docs.text:
Concord's Road Centerlines adapter is a Concord municipal source. It was not reused as though it described Walnut Creek streets.

Walnut Creek ROW research instead starts from Walnut Creek Engineering, current City plans/records, and any Walnut Creek-specific GIS layer later identified.

docs.title: Adjacent parcels
docs.text:
The same GIS-intersection method returned six non-target Walnut Creek parcels. Only one — City parcel 178-300-040 at 1375 Civic Drive — was strongly tied by independent evidence to the material Library/Civic Park question.

Architecture consequence:

intersection results are discovery candidates; they require human relevance screening before promotion.

docs.title: Recorded-map type aliases
docs.text:
The Walnut Creek assessor sheet used MB for historical subdivision references. The Concord-era recorded-map adapter had only been validated against LSM/record-of-survey and corner-record usage.

The initial Walnut Creek Book/Page query therefore failed to constrain the Record Type field even though it still returned identifiable book/page records.

The adapter was corrected to normalize:

  • LSM / RS → Record of Survey Map;
  • CR → Corner Record;
  • MB / subdivision → Subdivision Map;
  • PM / parcel → Parcel Map.

docs.title: Live post-fix verification
docs.text:
GitHub Actions run:

  • run ID: 35779391449
  • job ID: 106920689651
  • conclusion: success
  • artifact: facility-prep-walnut-creek-parcel
  • artifact ID: 10716842873
  • artifact ZIP SHA-256: 91f683b20188b3f70bb0480df8ef4cf014c399ee410f40fb4f70e3dc6d3432d4.

The corrected Rancho Dolores query generated:

([Recorded Maps Book]="2" AND [Recorded Maps Page]="36" AND [Record Type]="Subdivision Map")

and returned exactly one result:

  • 2M36
  • entry 482387
  • Subdivision Map
  • APN metadata 178 030
  • Walnut Creek
  • RANCHO DOLORES
  • recorded 7/26/1909.

The corrected Oak Park query likewise included Record Type = Subdivision Map and returned exactly one result:

  • 18M385
  • entry 128855
  • Subdivision Map
  • Walnut Creek
  • OAK PARK
  • recorded 3/4/1922.

This verifies that the fix changed the actual source query rather than merely changing local labels.

docs.title: Legal-analysis validation
docs.text:
Walnut Creek also validates the anchor-case comparator design.

The same site contains areas for which different analytic anchors are appropriate:

  • ordinary municipal sidewalk → ordinary sidewalk/Grace doctrine;
  • civic plaza, public entrance, open surface parking → Prigmore is a strong comparator;
  • public park → traditional park doctrine;
  • underground garage → Prigmore is not enough; Cornelius, Kokinda, Sammartano and general forum-purpose analysis become materially more important;
  • Oak View / Las Trampas opened room channels → Faith Center is the closer comparator;
  • study rooms / children's patio → separate purpose/access analysis.

The test therefore supports the rule:

generalize the comparator method, not a facility-type conclusion.

docs.title: Research-sufficiency validation
docs.text:
The assessor map exposed century-old subdivision references. Facility Prep resolved their identities, but current City planning/engineering/access sources are more likely to answer present plaza/ROW/garage questions.

The outcome-determinative boundary gate therefore works as intended: preserve the historical chain, but do not turn it into mandatory title archaeology unless a present boundary/easement dispute makes it material.

docs.title: Workflow state
docs.text:
The temporary Walnut Creek probe workflow was used with a branch-push trigger during live validation, then returned to manual-only execution after the final successful test. Before the Sweep 008 PR, the temporary workflow was removed from the branch entirely.

Machine-generated output remains artifact-only by default. Reviewed evidence is promoted manually into the facility evidence manifest.

The canonical .github/workflows/facility-prep.yml remains the retained prototype workflow; Walnut Creek's validation workflow is intentionally not promoted as a second permanent facility-specific workflow.

docs.title: Development consequence
docs.text:
After Concord + Walnut Creek, Facility Prep can reasonably treat the following as reusable architecture within Contra Costa County:

  • countywide parcel lookup/normalization;
  • assessor-map acquisition and preservation;
  • candidate-neighbor discovery plus human relevance screening;
  • Contra Costa Public Works recorded-map index adapter;
  • evidence-stage separation;
  • stop rules;
  • outcome-determinative boundary gate;
  • anchor-case comparator method.

Municipal AddressPoint, municipal road/ROW, owned-property, site-plan, parking, park, and facility-control sources remain modular enrichments.

The next architecture test should therefore be a materially different facility category, rather than pretending another library is necessary to prove every module universal.

docs.title: Walnut Creek Library — Policy Search Review
Sources reviewed
docs.text:
Current CCCL public-facing sources reviewed for Walnut Creek-specific access/recording/room rules include:

  • branch page: https://ccclib.org/locations/26/
  • CCCL policy portal: https://ccclib.org/policies/
  • current Patron Conduct Policy linked from the policy portal;
  • CCCL Rooms directory: https://ccclib.org/rooms/
  • Las Trampas policy: https://ccclib.org/las-trampas-room-policy/
  • Group Study Room rules: https://ccclib.org/walnut-creek-library-group-study-room-rules/
  • system Room Use PDF revised April 2025: https://ccclib.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/72/2026/03/LP-RMS-MeetingRoomRules_2025E_ADA.pdf
  • City Oak View page: https://www.walnutcreekartsrec.org/parks-facilities/facility-rentals/walnut-creek-library-oak-view-room

Targeted site searches for Walnut Creek + photography, video, filming, camera and recording did not locate a dedicated ordinary-patron camera rule.

docs.title: Photography / videography finding
docs.text:
Approved wording:

No dedicated public-facing Walnut Creek-specific ordinary-patron photography/videography rule was located in the online sources reviewed as of September 22, 2026.

Do not shorten this to there is no photography policy.

The finding does not establish:

  • absence of internal staff/security guidance;
  • absence of signs not reproduced online;
  • absence of program-specific or rental-specific media conditions;
  • absence of privacy or conduct rules applicable to particular conduct;
  • absence of a later-adopted policy.

docs.title: Current room-source discrepancy
docs.text:
The 2025-revised system Room Use PDF says arrangements for both Oak View and Las Trampas are through City Facility Rentals.

Current live sources now split the channels:

  • Oak View: City Facility Rentals;
  • Las Trampas: direct CCCL/online booking.

The current City Oak View page expressly says smaller rooms such as Las Trampas are reserved directly through CCCL and are not facilitated by the City rental office. Current CCCL Rooms/Las Trampas pages agree.

Working treatment:

CURRENT-LIVE-SOURCES-SUPPORT-CCCL-LAS-TRAMPAS-BOOKING / OLDER-PDF-DISCREPANCY-PRESERVED

The older PDF remains relevant history and could matter if a formal underlying control agreement is later disputed, but it should not silently override the newer mutually corroborating current-use sources.

docs.title: Study-room expression rule
docs.text:
Current Walnut Creek Group Study Room rules expressly prohibit:

  • advertising;
  • petitions;
  • solicitations;
  • sales.

This rule belongs to the study-room channel and must not be generalized to the ordinary Library interior, meeting rooms, civic plaza, sidewalks, park, or parking areas.

Its constitutional validity has not been finally adjudicated by this branch sweep. The room remains a purpose-limited channel requiring its own forum/rule analysis.

docs.title: Walnut Creek Library — Recorded Map Review
docs.text: Research date: 2026-09-22 Custodian: Contra Costa County Public Works Recorded Maps / Laserfiche WebLink Public search: https://records.pw.contra-costa.org/WebLink/CustomSearch.aspx?SearchName=RecordedMaps&dbid=0&repo=PWRecords

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Follow the historical map references printed on Assessor Book 178 Page 30 and determine whether the County's public recorded-map index contains facility-relevant records.

The search was performed through the same anonymous, read-only form/query/listing services used by the public WebLink client. No authentication, CAPTCHA, access-control, or paid-copy restriction was bypassed.

docs.title: 1. APN / assessor-book metadata search
docs.text:
Search field:

APN = 178 30

Result:

  • search generated successfully;
  • hitCount = 0;
  • failed = false.

Interpretation:

This establishes only that the Recorded Maps index did not return a record whose current indexed APN metadata exactly matched 178 30. It is not proof that no relevant recorded map exists. Historical subdivision maps may predate modern APNs, may carry older assessor-book formatting, or may be discoverable only by book/page, tract/subdivision, permit, or geographic metadata.

docs.title: 2. Rancho Dolores — assessor reference MB 2-36
docs.text:
The first probe searched Book 2, Page 36. Because the then-current adapter did not yet map the user-facing MB alias to the WebLink option Subdivision Map, the initial query was broader than intended and returned four record types sharing that book/page.

Human relevance screening identified one exact match to the assessor annotation:

  • name: 2M36
  • entry ID: 482387
  • record type: Subdivision Map
  • APN metadata: 178 030
  • city: Walnut Creek
  • date recorded: 7/26/1909
  • subdivision name: RANCHO DOLORES
  • Book: 2
  • Page: 36

This independently verifies the identity of the historical subdivision reference printed on Assessor Book 178 Page 30.

The other Book 2/Page 36 hits had different record types and/or APN/geographic metadata and were not promoted as facility evidence merely because the book/page numbers coincided.

docs.title: 3. Oak Park — assessor reference MB 18-385
docs.text:
The Book 18, Page 385 search returned one record:

  • name: 18M385
  • entry ID: 128855
  • page count: 2
  • city: Walnut Creek
  • date recorded: 3/4/1922
  • engineer/surveyor: CLYDE LAIRD
  • permit: SD1922-01083
  • record type: Subdivision Map
  • Book: 18
  • Page: 385
  • road vicinity: MAIN ST, SPENCER, LINCOLN AVE, CAMPLIN AVE, DEWING WAY
  • subdivision name: OAK PARK

This exactly corresponds to the OAK PARK SUB'N MB 18-385 3/4/1922 annotation on the assessor sheet.

docs.title: 4. Adapter lesson and correction
docs.text:
Sweep 008 exposed a useful generalization defect in laserfiche_recorded_map_lookup.py.

The Concord prototype had only needed aliases for:

  • LSM / record of survey;
  • CR / corner record.

When Walnut Creek introduced old assessor annotations using MB, the adapter accepted the argument but failed to select the WebLink Record Type = Subdivision Map option. The book/page query itself remained valid and the relevant records could be screened manually, but the request was not as narrowly constrained as intended.

The adapter was corrected during Sweep 008 to support:

  • LSM / RS → Record of Survey;
  • CR → Corner Record;
  • MB / subdivision → Subdivision Map;
  • PM / parcel → Parcel Map.

This is precisely why the Facility Prep SOP requires a second same-category validation before treating a jurisdiction adapter as generalized.

docs.title: 5. Evidentiary value
docs.text:
Current status:

  • Rancho Dolores map identity: OFFICIAL-INDEX-RESOLVED / HISTORICAL-CHAIN-RELEVANT
  • Oak Park map identity: OFFICIAL-INDEX-RESOLVED / HISTORICAL-CHAIN-RELEVANT
  • present Library parcel geometry: not established by these historical records alone
  • present North Broadway/Lincoln ROW: UNRESOLVED by these records
  • present plaza/parking/garage control: UNRESOLVED by these records

The recorded-map search should therefore not become an archaeological detour. Current City plans, engineering/ROW sources, and current operational documents have greater potential to change the present forum/removal analysis.

Under the outcome-determinative boundary gate, deeper retrieval of these century-old subdivision maps should be pursued only if a current disputed boundary/easement question makes their contents material.

docs.title: Walnut Creek Library — Self-Service Sunday Status
docs.text:
Reviewed: 2026-09-22

Current CCCL Self-Service Sunday FAQ:

https://ccclib.org/faq/meeting/

As of this review, CCCL states that Self-Service Sundays are currently provided at:

  • Concord Library;
  • San Pablo Library;

with Pittsburg listed as coming soon.

Walnut Creek is not listed as a participating Self-Service Sunday branch. The current Walnut Creek branch page lists Sunday as closed.

Accordingly, Sweep 008 does not import Concord's special card/PIN Sunday access regime into Walnut Creek.

Status:

NO-CURRENT-SELF-SERVICE-SUNDAY-ACCESS-LOCATED / ORDINARY-SUNDAY-CLOSED

This is a current service-status finding, not a permanent claim. It should be reverified if CCCL expands the program.
